source.title: Through the Bottleneck: How Multi-head Latent Attention Separates Content from Position in Language Models
source.authors: S. Dhruvil; Fenil Sojitra; R. Chauhan

record.tranche_reason: The study measures induction-pattern attention heads in a 114.1M-parameter MLA transformer, an architecture setting different from the cited standard-MHA work.
record.gate_note: The head taxonomy reports induction and previous-token scores and identifies the detected heads. The comparison with standard MHA is cited from Olsson et al. (2022), not measured here. The study does not measure training-time formation, in-context-learning loss by token position, or few-shot task learning.
record.test_reason: The study scores all 192 heads of a 114.1M-parameter MLA transformer (not attention-only) for induction and previous-token attention patterns. It detects five induction heads, which bears on V4 (induction heads in another architecture). Composition, copying and training dynamics are not measured, so V1–V3 and V5–V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that all five detected induction heads sit at Layer 12 of their MLA model, with previous-token heads earlier. They hypothesise the shared cKV bottleneck constrains circuit topology, but call this an initial single-model, single-seed result needing matched MHA baselines and multi-seed replication. The contrast with MHA is a qualitative comparison to Olsson et al., not a controlled one.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes a pretrained-then-fine-tuned MLA model using attention-pattern scores; it does not reproduce the original study's training and measurement setup.

fits_no_version.finding: All five detected induction heads co-locate at Layer 12. The authors contrast this with induction heads distributed across layers in MHA, but that comparison is cited from Olsson et al., not measured with a matched baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In MLA transformers, the shared KV bottleneck concentrates induction heads in a single layer rather than spreading them across layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer 12, which holds the induction heads, has only a moderate cKV disruption-attribution score (0.50, against 1.00 at Layer 15). This is a correlational signal, not a causal test of induction heads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layers holding induction heads are not the layers whose KV representations most affect next-token predictions.

record.problems: One model and one training run; no matched MHA baseline; head taxonomy uses TinyStories passages; the induction scores measure attention patterns without a direct causal test of composition or copying.

untested.parts: Not tested. There is no composition or copying test, the model is not attention-only, and the 'pipeline' is asserted from co-occurring head types only.
Not tested. Only a final checkpoint is analysed; there is no training dynamics, abruptness or loss bump.
Not tested. Loss by token index and the share of in-context learning due to induction heads are not measured.
Untested parts: other MLA sizes, seeds, training runs, model families and modalities, and a matched MHA model.
Not tested. No data or training setup is varied.
Not tested. No few-shot task learning is measured.
Not tested. Formation is not observed.

missing.what: The induction-score threshold or criterion used to classify heads as induction heads, and the score distribution for all other heads (no random or chance baseline is given).

record.verdict_notes: The model is a full 24-layer transformer, not attention-only, so V1 is not tested. The co-location finding concerns topology, which no version covers. There is an internal inconsistency: the text says previous-token heads are in L1–L5, but Table 3 lists L10 H6. The analysis is on the fine-tuned checkpoint only.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures induction-pattern attention and previous-token heads, but does not causally demonstrate composition between them or show that the heads copy the predicted next token. It does not establish that the model is an attention-only transformer.
Formation over training, abruptness, in-context-learning gain, and a coincident training-loss bump are not measured.
The study does not measure loss by token index or the proportion of large-transformer in-context learning attributable to induction heads.
Only one MLA model and one training run are studied; other model families, sizes, runs, architectures, and modalities are not tested.
There is no comparison of data or training setups, or measurement of how they affect induction formation or in-context learning.
The study does not assess few-shot task learning or compare induction heads with other mechanisms as carriers of that learning.
The study analyzes head patterns in a trained checkpoint, not the sequence or number of transitions during formation.
